title: Seedance 2.5 on a blender fork
author: Pradyumgg
selftext:
Seedance 2.5 just shipped, and we wired it into Mixar, which is a Blender fork. The scene you build is the input, so the set, props, and lighting stay fixed across generations instead of drifting every time you re-roll for a new angle.

You get full camera control, push in, orbit, track, whatever the shot needs, and you go from blockout to finished render without leaving the editor.

Clip attached is straight out of it. Happy to answer questions on how the scene data gets passed through.

comments.author: hippohaul
comments.body: Super cool, would love to try it.  How can it be accessed?

replies.author: Pradyumgg
replies.body:
Thanks. You can access mixar at [https://www.mixar.app](https://www.mixar.app) 

Let me know if you have any further questions!

comments.body: Awesome! How can we use this?

replies.author: Pradyumgg
replies.body: You can give it a swirl at [https://www.mixar.app](https://www.mixar.app)

replies.author: Pradyumgg
replies.body: Haha, it's time for your scene to become the prompt!

comments.author: OinkLikeAPig
comments.body: Looks incredible and my mind on what I want to create is already racing

replies.author: Pradyumgg
replies.body: There's endless possibilities with seedance 2.5's clay render support. We can have our entire scene as a prompt!

comments.author: Macaroon-Guilty
comments.body: Oh wow, well done. Does it take in depth map or just clay render? What's the cost for this clip? How many attempts?

replies.author: Pradyumgg
replies.body:
It does take in both depth map and clay render. you can use keyframes as well. 

seedance 2.5 at 720p costs about 0.5$ per second. so somewhere closer to 15$ for the video. It is kinda expensive, but at 480p output the price is less than half of that.

Made this in one shot via Mixar!  
[https://www.mixar.app](https://www.mixar.app)
